title: 可拆解的 3D 相机镜头交互网页
summary: 用代码程序化生成镜筒、镜片和六叶片光圈，做出可旋转查看的 3D 镜头：光圈滑块 f/1.7–f/22 联动叶片开合，Studio / Exploded / Section 三种视图，加光线路径演示，交付离线单文件 HTML。

source.title: AI 生成 3D 模型网页怎么做？AutoClaw 可拆解镜头
source.original_setup: AutoClaw（原文未注明专家与模型），交付 React 18 + TypeScript 项目和约 731 KB 单文件 HTML
source.notes: 提示词照原文英文原句。原文交付 React + TypeScript 工程和打包后的单文件版；这里没有构建工具也不能加载第三方库，只交付手写 3D 渲染的单文件 HTML，没有 React 工程源码。

turns.label: 需求
turns.prompt: Build a complete, runnable React and TypeScript web app featuring an interactive 3D camera lens. Model the lens and a six-blade iris procedurally in code. Add an aperture slider, orbit controls, an exploded view, a cross-section view and visible light rays. All parts must remain aligned when switching views.
turns.reply_html:
I've built Lens Lab, an interactive 3D model of a 35 mm-class prime lens, as a single file: lens-lab.html.

React and TypeScript were not used. This environment can't load React or run a TypeScript compiler, and the file has to work offline on its own. So the app is written in plain JavaScript and WebGL, but split into the same parts a React app would have: a small state store, <LensModel/>, <IrisDiaphragm/>, <RayTracer/>, <Viewport/>, <OrbitControls/> and <ControlPanel/>. That structure would carry over to React directly.

What's in it

  • Lens modelled in code: four glass elements built from real lens surface curves, plus two barrel sections, a spacer, a ridged focus ring, an aperture ring, a bayonet mount with three lugs, and a sensor.
  • Six-blade iris: each blade's inner edge sits exactly at the current opening size, so together they form the hexagonal opening. The blades overlap one another like a real iris and rotate slightly as they close.
  • Aperture slider: sets f/1.8 to f/22 (smooth, or jump to standard stops). It shows the opening's diameter, the exposure change and how many rays get through. The blades reshape live.
  • Orbit controls: drag to rotate, right-drag or Shift+drag to pan, scroll to zoom, double-click to reset. There are also camera presets (3/4, side, front, top).
  • Exploded view: every part slides only along the lens's central axis, so nothing can move off-centre.
    • The panel shows "Coaxial deviation", computed live from the parts' sideways offsets (always 0).
    • Parts are labelled in this view.
  • Cross-section: an animated cut through the centre. Cut faces show as hatched metal and light-blue glass.
  • Light rays: traced in real time through the actual element positions, using the refraction law at each surface.
    • Gold rays come in straight along the axis; cyan rays come in at an angle you set with the "Off-axis field angle" slider.
    • Rays blocked by the iris or a lens edge are dimmed.
    • Rays stay faintly visible through the housing even when the barrel isn't cut away.

Keyboard shortcuts: E exploded, C cross-section, R rays, A axis, O auto-rotate.

turns.label: Self-check
turns.prompt: 这是你刚交付的网页在无头 Chrome 中打开后的截图。像交付前预览检查一样看：文字重叠或被截断、布局错位、中文显示成方框、画面空白、控件看不见。再回读你的代码，确认每个可见控件都接上了事件处理、核心交互能走通。需要修改就用同名文件交付完整的修正版；已经可以交付就用一两句话说明，不交付文件。
turns.reply_html:
The screenshot shows the app never drew anything: the screenshot browser has no WebGL, so the page stopped at the "WebGL is not available" message, and the stat boxes and HUD readouts stayed at "—".

I've rewritten the 3D display to work without WebGL. It now draws the scene itself onto a standard 2D canvas, so it works in any browser, offline.

  • Same look and behaviour:
    • Glass is still see-through.
    • The cross-section still animates, with hatched cut faces.
    • Light rays still show faintly through solid parts.
  • Smoothness: while you drag or a transition is running, it renders at lower resolution for speed, then redraws sharp once things stop. When nothing changes, it doesn't redraw at all.
  • Unchanged: the lens model, iris, ray trace and controls work exactly as before. Every part still moves only along the central axis, so parts stay aligned when switching views.

I haven't seen this version render yet; a new screenshot will confirm it.
